description: The post-Draft workflow's example set (US-ME08, F5), in the marketingskills evals.json shape: each example's prompt, the output expected, its assertions, and its files. An example that carries `run` is re-run by the agent on every change to the post-Draft Instructions (US-ME16, ADR 0003): its session drafts the calendar days `run` names in a throwaway lab built from `lab` and the example's own overlays, and its deterministic assertions are read off what the launcher took in. An example's first file, if it has one, is a candidate Draft the unit tests (src/tests/test_examples.py) check against the synthetic kit in files/mandu and the code in files/code; a second file is the Draft of its A/B pair's reference leg. A judged assertion is judged by nothing: the notice of a change lists it for the Founder.

assertion_kinds.deterministic: check is one of: passes; blocked_by (rule: a finding's rule, or the start of one); not_blocked_by (rule); warns (rule); cites_angle (angle); hook_frozen; lint_passes; each of a re-run example for its day, or the day it names; and, for a re-run example only, queued (item: a kind; count; cites: words each queued item holds), nothing_queued (item), nothing_set_aside
assertion_kinds.judged: text is a statement of the agent's Draft that no check decides; nothing judges it, and the notice of an Instructions change lists it as not judged

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3 of window 1 (P03 / AB-2 leg A, primary YouTube Shorts) from the brief.
evals.expected_output: A Draft that passes every check: the frozen Hook opens the video and every caption, both platforms carry identical text but for the call-to-action line that ends each caption with its platform's Waitlist address, the one behavioral claim shows the code that supports it, and the item cites Angle P03, its sourced pain, signal, and kill criterion.

assertions.text: The captions read as calm and plain, in the brand's voice, with no hype.
The hook beat's visual action, spoken line, and on-screen text do not repeat each other.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 1 of window 1 (P01 / AB-1 leg A, primary TikTok) from the brief.
evals.expected_output: A Draft that passes every check and cites Angle P01, with a claim located in the code at the commit read.

assertions.text: Every behavioral claim the copy makes appears under Claims.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below put a banned word in its caption.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft and names the banned-word rule; it never reaches the Review Queue.

assertions.text: A good Draft states the mechanic plainly without bro-fitness words.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below claims a number of people who use the app.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft for invented proof: the product has no users, and a Draft leaves [NEED: source] rather than filling a number in.

assertions.text: A good Draft lets the demo be the only proof.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below names a competitor.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft, naming the competitor and the research file that names it.

assertions.text: A good Draft states the product's own mechanics only.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below changed one word of the frozen Hook.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft: the Hook differs from its frozen text in ab-pairs.md, and a change to a Hook enters only as a new Angle through a package-change proposal.

assertions.text: A good Draft that thinks the Hook should change says so as a package-change proposal instead.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 1; the candidate below states the unmeasured speed claim.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft on the checklist's benchmark line until the real-device measurement exists.

assertions.text: A good Draft shows speed only as the screen visibly shows it, with no number.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 5 (P05), whose Angle rests on the unmeasured speed claim.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft even with no number in its copy, since its Angle depends on the claim the checklist still holds open.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below carries six hashtags.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft on TikTok's hashtag limit from config/platforms.json.

assertions.text: A good Draft uses at most the one hashtag the kit's drafts use.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below repeats another Angle's Hook in its caption.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft: a Hook belongs to exactly one Angle.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below cites code lines that do not show its claim.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft: the cited lines at the commit read do not contain the quoted code.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 8 (P01 / AB-1 leg B), whose other leg, day 1, already has an open post from the second file; the candidate below also reworded the second caption line.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks day 8's Draft and names the field that differs: an A/B leg matches its reference leg in everything but the Hook. Day 1's open post stands.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below opens a line with a stock AI phrase.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft, naming the stock phrase.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below adds an urgency line.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft for fake scarcity.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below runs one caption sentence long.
evals.expected_output: The Draft passes, with long-sentence warnings shown to the Founder; a warning never blocks.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 2 of window 1 (P02, primary TikTok); its frozen Hook says the app does something no code at the commit read does.
evals.expected_output: A Draft that keeps the frozen Hook and lists the Hook's claim under Claims with Code: none, so the launcher blocks it naming that claim; the supported claim listed beside it never stands in for it. A package-change proposal cites the Hook and the code.

assertions.text: Every behavioral claim the copy makes appears under Claims, the Hook's included, and no listed claim is one the Draft does not make.
A package-change proposal cites the frozen Hook and the code that lacks the behavior, and the Hook is unchanged.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 4 of window 1 (P04, primary YouTube Shorts) from the brief.
evals.expected_output: A Draft that passes every check: the frozen Hook opens it, the offline claim shows the code that builds a session on the device, and the item cites Angle P04.

assertions.text: The video plan shows airplane mode switched on before the session appears, in one take with no cuts.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 6 of window 1 (P06, primary TikTok) from the brief.
evals.expected_output: A Draft that passes every check and cites Angle P06; its Hook makes no behavioral claim, so it claims nothing the code would have to show.

assertions.text: The captions say plainly what is on screen, with no hype word and no AI tell.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 7 of window 1 (P07, primary TikTok) from the brief.
evals.expected_output: A Draft that passes every check and cites Angle P07, planned as the timer timelapse its Format names.

assertions.text: Nothing in the video plan asks for footage the Angle's Format does not name.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Drafts for days 6 and 7 of window 1, both due in one run.
evals.expected_output: Two Drafts, each passing every check and citing its own Angle; neither borrows the other's Hook.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3 of window 1, where the brand rules now ban a word the frozen Hook holds.
evals.expected_output: A Draft that keeps the frozen Hook word for word, so the launcher blocks it on the banned word, and one package-change proposal that cites both the Hook and the brand rule; the agent never rewords a frozen Hook to pass.

assertions.text: The proposal leaves to the Founder which side changes, the Hook or the rule.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 1 of window 1, while an open checklist line blocks everything public.
evals.expected_output: A Draft written as the kit requires, which the launcher blocks naming the open checklist line, and one package-change proposal that cites the line.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below ends neither caption with the call-to-action line the brief gives.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft naming the call-to-action rule and, for each platform, the line its caption must end with.

assertions.text: A good Draft ends each caption with its platform's line, word for word, after the pre-launch status.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below words its call to action its own way instead of the brief's line.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft: only the line brand-rules.json gives, word for word, may end a caption.

assertions.text: A good Draft copies the call-to-action line from the brief rather than rewording it.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below ends its TikTok caption with YouTube's Waitlist address.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft naming the Source the address belongs to, so no TikTok sign-up is counted as YouTube's.

assertions.text: A good Draft gives each platform its own address, so the Founder sees which channel brought each sign-up.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below adds a second line with a link before each caption's call to action.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft: the call-to-action line is the post's one call to action and only link.

assertions.text: A good Draft asks the viewer for one thing only.

evals.prompt: Prepare the Draft for day 3; the candidate below shows the call-to-action line as on-screen text in its last beat.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft naming the beat: the call to action goes in the caption text only, never on the video.

assertions.text: A good Draft keeps the call to action in the caption text, never on the video.
